items.title: Nepal’s fossil fuel push clashes with its clean energy ambitions
items.desc: As the country seeks climate finance and promotes hydropower exports, new petroleum pipeline projects risk locking it into decades of fossil fuel dependence.

items.title: Constitutional Bench resumes hearings after weeks of deadlock
items.desc: Seniority-based appointments end the discord lasting a month-and-a-half. The bench has 246 cases to hear, including some pending for eight years.

items.title: Kathmandu’s evicted squatters say they have no proper food, medical care at temporary centres
items.desc: Displaced families are being asked to leave holding centres without secure housing, adequate food or access to essential healthcare.

items.title: PM’s advisers turn political controversy into Facebook banter
items.desc: The prime minister’s inner circle has joined online jokes and memes about the Inam Sapkota phone controversy, drawing criticism for trivialising questions of accountability.

items.title: The National Games in Karnali must mark a new beginning
items.desc: Karnali must sustain the momentum, maintain its facilities and nurture young talent to build a lasting sporting culture.

items.title: Was PM Shah’s visit to India really grand, or was it illusory?
items.desc: Modi would have been quite relieved that Shah was more interested in cricket than brickbats.

items.title: Keep Himalayan settlements out of harm’s way
items.desc: Monitoring and early warnings alone are insufficient without context-sensitive settlement planning.

items.title: Kenyan cult leader serving 200-year murder sentence convicted of new charges
items.desc: Mackenzie led an apocalyptic Christian church in a forest near Kenya’s Indian Ocean coast, telling his followers to starve themselves and their ​children to reach heaven before the end of the world.

items.title: The man who took Nepal to Lord’s now wants a British PM in Nepal
items.desc: Prashanta Kunwar pitched a Nepal match at the home of cricket when few would listen. Now he has asked a British prime minister to visit Nepal.

items.title: Bangladesh minimum wage hike misses garment workers’ demands, sparks fresh protests
items.desc: Workers had initially sought a minimum wage of 32,000 taka ($257) before lowering their demand to 18,000 taka during negotiations. Factory owners first proposed 15,000 taka and later raised their offer to 17,000.

items.title: Supreme Court declines interim order in Dan Bahadur Karki’s petition
items.desc: The court has directed an expedited hearing, citing the importance and sensitivity of leadership and the chain of command within the Nepal Police.

items.title: Election Commission updates Nepali Congress leadership and amended statute
items.desc: The commission has formally recognised the party’s new 231-member central committee, elected at its 15th general convention, and amendments to its statute.

items.title: Lack of accommodation holds back Khaptad tourism
items.desc: Two government-built lodges with 100 beds remain closed two years after handover, leaving visitors with few places to stay and limiting the destination’s tourism potential.

items.title: Possible Tesla merger could aid SpaceX’s S&P 500 entry, J.P. Morgan says
items.desc: Analysts say a merger with Tesla could help SpaceX bypass some S&P 500 eligibility requirements, while the gradual release of locked-up shares could bring it closer to inclusion in major indexes.

items.title: Army open National Games campaign with 3-0 win over Lumbini
items.desc: Bharat Khawas and Laken Limbu scored before an own goal sealed Tribhuvan Army Club’s victory in the men’s football tournament.

items.title: Clear skies reveal a sweep of Himalayan peaks from Namo Buddha
items.desc: Ganesh, Langtang, Jugal, Dorje Lakpa and Gaurishankar are among the ranges visible from the hilltop in Kavrepalanchok.

items.title: The killings have a name: Femicide. Nepal’s law does not recognise it
items.desc: An investigation of 489 homicide cases across all 77 districts identified 107 femicides — more than one in five. Most victims had endured domestic violence before they were killed. Yet Nepal has no separate legal category or official count for such killings.

items.title: Attack on Riyadh financial centre injures 11, including Nepalis
items.desc: Saudi Civil Defence blamed Yemen’s Houthi rebels for Tuesday’s attack, but did not disclose how many Nepalis were among the injured or their condition.

items.title: China’s Huawei convicted in sprawling US criminal trial over Iran business
items.desc: A New York jury finds the Chinese telecommunications giant guilty of 10 criminal counts, including bank fraud, sanctions violations and conspiring to steal trade secrets from US companies.

items.title: Why India-Pakistan cricket matches keep coming despite political tensions
items.desc: Indian government policy continues to rule out bilateral sporting ties, even as participation in multilateral events remains permissible. The International Cricket Council and the Asian Cricket Council have exploited this distinction with remarkable efficiency.

items.title: How documentary cinema captures a South Asia in transit
items.desc: This year’s Film Southasia brings together documentaries that explore migration, fractured histories, cultural resilience and political resistance across the subcontinent.

items.title: 10th National Games kick off with two national records shattered in swimming
items.desc: Bishal Kumal and Lily Bohra bettered the records in 50m breaststroke and women’s 400m individual medley, respectively.

items.title: Buddha Air revives plan to launch international jet flights from Pokhara
items.desc: New air routes and satellite-based navigation could improve connectivity, but the bigger challenge will be attracting enough passengers to make the underused airport commercially viable.

items.title: Three months on, flood-hit communities in Nuwakot remain cut off from district headquarters
items.desc: The delay in installing a Bailey bridge over the Trishuli river in Bidur has forced thousands to walk for hours to access government services.

items.title: AI detection woes drive students to court. Universities search for answers
items.desc: Students fear that even their original work could be flagged as AI-generated. This has also raised questions about how much trust should be placed in detection software.

items.title: National Games put Karnali’s sporting ambitions to test
items.desc: For a province associated with poverty and remoteness, hosting the National Games is a chance to present a different picture.

items.title: Prioritise action against both online and offline gender-based violence
items.desc: Addressing technology-facilitated violence against women requires challenging patriarchal norms that normalise abuse.
